attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, rebutting Newton in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Can be misused' states a present capability, not a hedged prediction like may or might. The proposition matches the statement: being stupid does not rule out being dangerous, and the propaganda and deepfake examples are kept.

contract.note: Documented 2024 misuse is a fair, ordinary test of a capability claim. The contract does not require proof of reach or harm, which matches the words 'can be misused'. Choosing a 2024 window does not change the result.

evidence.note: A US regulator release dated May 2024 documents a generative-AI voice deepfake of Biden used for election misinformation in January 2024.
OpenAI threat report from May 2024 (a company disclosure, but about misuse of its own models) describes state-linked operations producing political propaganda with its models.
Little extra reach bears on how much harm was done, not on whether misuse was possible or happened.

reviews.rationale: Primary records from 2024, before the post, show generative AI used for a deepfake (FCC) and for propaganda (OpenAI report). That meets the support condition. The low reach reported is outside what the claim asserts.

attribution.note: Marcus's own numbered statement of his views in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithful. 'Despite their limits' is kept as a qualifier. The separate point about imminent military misuse is rightly left out.

contract.note: 'Dangerous' has no threshold. Reading it as concrete risk of material harm, shown by demonstrated discriminatory behavior or actual misuse, is an ordinary reading and not stretched either way.

evidence.note: March 2024 preprint shows LLMs give harmful dialect-based outputs in job and sentencing tasks. This is experimental evidence of risk, not measured real-world injury.
Company disclosure documents actual use of LLMs by covert influence operations. Low reach is noted, but under the contract low impact does not disprove danger.

reviews.rationale: Both legs of the support condition are met before publication: experimental evidence of covert racist LLM decisions, and documented LLM use in deceptive influence operations. The low reach reported does not meet the contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words. The leaders' statements are the evidence, not claims attributed to him.

semantics.note: The surrounding text (CEOs 'reached similar conclusions' on LLM limitations) supports reading 'what I foresaw' as his predicted LLM and scaling limits.

contract.note: The result depends on the drafter's reading of 'what I foresaw' (the 2022 diminishing-returns essay) and of 'bear out'. Both are reasonable given the context about LLM limitations and are not stretched. The essay is used only as a baseline.

evidence.note: Andreessen, early November 2024: LLMs are hitting the same ceiling, a 'local topping out'.
Pichai at DealBook on December 4, 2024: progress will get harder and needs deeper breakthroughs. The article is dated after the post but before the evaluation date.
Nadella at Ignite, November 2024: scaling laws are empirical observations, not physical laws. Publication date is approximate.
Pointing to test-time compute is not a statement that scaling continues unabated, so it does not meet the contradiction condition. It is consistent with 'new ideas needed'.
Marcus's own 2022 essay. It fixes what he predicted and is not proof that he was right.

reviews.rationale: All three leaders made statements in the window that acknowledge limits, slowing progress or doubt about continued scaling gains, in line with his 2022 prediction. Nadella's mention of test-time compute does not amount to a claim that scaling continues unabated.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'daily', 'write term papers' and the hedged parenthetical (marked 'perhaps'). It is right not to score the parenthetical.

contract.note: The contract stretches the claim in the speaker's favor. It reads 'daily' as merely habitual and counts any AI help with assessments, including tutor-style concept explanations, as writing term papers. A fair reading needs frequent use of LLMs to produce paper text.

evidence.note: 2024 Stack Overflow survey: 62% of developers currently use AI tools. This fits 'coders use it a lot'.
53% of UK undergraduates used AI to help with assessments, but mostly as a tutor. Only 13% generated text for assessments. This only partly supports 'write term papers'.
The HEPI author says students use AI in limited ways rather than having it write their essays. This cuts against the writing part of the claim.
Pew teen survey reported January 2025, fieldwork dates unknown: 26% used ChatGPT for schoolwork. Not specific to term papers or daily use.

reviews.rationale: The coder part holds (62% of developers use AI tools). The student part is only partly borne out: many students use AI for assessments, but only 13% generate text, HEPI says most do not have AI write their essays, and no source measures daily use for papers. The contract's loose reading would make it look fully supported.
